coding_notes: Include agricultural cross-border trade; extension beyond the core topics 16, 18 and 19.

Use Other/unclear for substantive cross-border migration, refugee or citizenship policy; use Not foreign policy for purely domestic administration. Migration is outside the four substantive course labels.
Include only substantive cross-border military policy; purely domestic defence administration is Not foreign policy.
Includes defence cooperation, security alliances and UN peacekeeping; military content takes priority over diplomacy as an instrument.
Include international military intelligence, espionage and covert operations; purely domestic administration is Not foreign policy.
Include military capabilities tied to international security; purely domestic administration is Not foreign policy.
Include nuclear deterrence, proliferation and arms control; purely domestic administration is Not foreign policy.
Includes military assistance and controls on arms sales abroad; weapons exports take security rather than trade or civilian aid.
Include personnel issues with a substantive international military focus; domestic personnel, pensions and veterans' administration are Not foreign policy.
Include procurement with a substantive international military focus; routine domestic purchasing is Not foreign policy.
Include foreign basing and international military access; domestic construction or land management is Not foreign policy.
Include international deployment or security cooperation involving reserves; domestic reserve administration is Not foreign policy.
Include international military environmental obligations; domestic waste disposal is Not foreign policy. Inspect the dominant issue before applying the proposed label.
Include substantive international security responses; domestic civil defence and homeland-security administration are Not foreign policy.
Include a substantive international military focus; domestic civilian employment and base closure policy are Not foreign policy.
Include a substantive international military focus; domestic contracting oversight is Not foreign policy.
Includes overseas war-related military operations, prisoners of war and civilian consequences of military operations.
Include claims tied to international military operations; domestic compensation administration is Not foreign policy.
Include international military research cooperation or an explicit international-security objective; domestic research administration is Not foreign policy.
Read the statement: use Security/defence if the military issue and cross-border scope are clear; Not foreign policy if domestic; otherwise Other/unclear.

Include international scientific cooperation as an additional foreign-policy issue; do not automatically treat scientific cooperation as diplomacy. Purely domestic technology transfer is Not foreign policy.
General cross-border trade policy; use the substantive object rather than negotiation as the classification rule.
Trade negotiations, agreements and disputes remain trade even when diplomacy is the instrument.
Export policy; military assistance and arms-transfer controls instead take Security/defence when military content dominates.
Use trade for cross-border investment and market-access policy under a broader international-commerce definition; otherwise Other/unclear.
Include trade-related competitiveness and external economic relations; purely domestic productivity policy is Not foreign policy.
Tariffs, import barriers and import regulation; tariff agreements can overlap with 1802 but share the same course label.
Use trade when exchange-rate policy substantively concerns cross-border commerce; other international monetary policy is Other/unclear and purely domestic policy is Not foreign policy.
Use trade if the cross-border commerce issue is identifiable; otherwise Other/unclear. Confirm foreign-policy scope from the text.
General international affairs can span diplomacy, aid and other issues; assign a substantive course label only when the statement supports it.
Civilian assistance abroad, including humanitarian relief; military assistance instead takes Security/defence.
International resource governance is outside the four substantive labels; use trade or diplomacy only if that is the dominant issue.
Use Aid only for civilian development assistance; a statement about a developing country is not automatically aid. Reclassify by its substantive issue.
Use Aid for development assistance or concessional development finance; other international finance and sovereign-debt issues are Other/unclear unless another substantive course label fits.
Use Diplomacy for European political or institutional relations; substantive EU trade, military or aid policy takes the corresponding label. Domestic implementation alone is Not foreign policy.
Use Diplomacy for bilateral political relations; references to a foreign country alone are insufficient. Reclassify trade, military and aid content by its substantive object.
International human-rights policy is outside the four substantive labels; negotiation or assistance takes another label only if it dominates the statement.
Use Diplomacy for international institutional relations; an organization's involvement alone does not establish the issue. Reclassify military, trade, aid or other substantive content accordingly.
Use Security/defence for military or defence responses to international terrorism; international criminal-law or policing cooperation is Other/unclear under the current narrow security definition.

Use Diplomacy for diplomatic relations, mediation and embassy affairs; passport or visa administration alone may be Not foreign policy. Negotiation about trade, military matters or aid follows the substantive-object rule.
Residual international affairs; assign a substantive course label only when the statement supports it. Keep uncertainty separate from the assigned label.
